Theme

Latin word

ars

ars, artis f.

noun, third declension

a profession, an art (medicine, law, teaching); skill; a craft, a trade; an art, a body of knowledge with its rules; skill, technique; the rules of an art; a handbook of an art; a treatise; an art, its rules and principles; a skill; the craft or profession one lives by

Examples

  • quibus autem artibus aut prūdentia major inest aut nōn mediocris ūtilitās quaeritur, ut medicīna, ut architectūra, ut doctrīna rērum honestārum, hae sunt iīs, quōrum ōrdinī conveniunt, honestae

    but the professions that call for more wisdom or bring no small benefit, such as medicine, architecture and the teaching of honourable things, are honourable for those whose station they suitCic. Off. 1.151 (Lewis & Short, s.v. ars)

    In the entry for profession

  • Ars illī sua cēnsus erat. Cum trāderet artem, «accipe quās habeō, studiī successor et hērēs,» dīxit «opēs.»

    His skill was his whole fortune. When he handed it on, he said: “Take what wealth I have, my successor and heir in the trade.”Ov. Met. 3.588–590

  • Nec vērō habēre virtūtem satis est quasi artem aliquam, nisi ūtāre; etsī ars quidem, cum eā nōn ūtāre, scientiā tamen ipsā tenērī potest, virtūs in ūsū suī tōta posita est

    Nor is it enough to have virtue as one has some art, unless you use it; for an art, even when you do not use it, can still be held by knowledge alone, but virtue lies wholly in its useCic. Rep. 1.2
